app.title: Washing Machine Navi
app.tagline: Find the right washing machine for your apartment, side by side.
app.subtagline: Built for Japanese rentals and apartments. Enter your waterproof pan size and tap type to instantly see which machines actually fit.

fit.heading: ① Enter your install space
fit.description: Enter your waterproof pan size and space dimensions, and the comparison table below will show which machines fit.
fit.heightHelp: Only needed if there's a shelf, vent fan, or low ceiling above limiting height. For a top-load machine this should be enough room for the lid to fully open, not just the closed body — we'll flag it when a model's lid-open height isn't confirmed. Leave blank if unsure.
fit.tapSingle: Single tap (cold water only — most common in rentals)
fit.helperTitle: What's a 防水パン (waterproof pan)?
fit.helperBody: A shallow tray installed under the washing machine to catch leaks. Always compare using its inner (usable) dimensions, not the outer size. Most rentals already have one installed, and 640×640mm is the most common size.
fit.useOldTitle: 🧺 Not sure of your exact space?
fit.useOldDescription: Use one of your saved old machines as a stand-in size instead.
fit.useOldEmpty: You haven't logged an old machine yet.
fit.useOldEmptyLink: Add one below to use it here ↓
fit.usingOldMachineNote: Using {{name}}'s size as a reference — your actual space may be a little larger, so treat these results as approximate.
fit.oldMachineLidNote: This height is your old machine's own closed body height, not a measured ceiling/shelf limit — it isn't used to check lid-open clearance. If you have a specific overhead limit, replace the height above with that number to check it.

recommend.typeVerticalHint: Washes powerfully, stays compact, costs less
recommend.typeDrumHint: Saves water, dries well, usually deeper

explain.dryHeatPump: It has proper heat-pump drying, so laundry comes out fully dry without you needing to hang it.
explain.drySimple: It includes simple drying — handy on rainy days when you can't hang laundry outside.
explain.noDryBudget: It skips the drying function, which keeps the price down since you said you don't need one.
explain.typeMatchVertical: It's a vertical (top-load) machine, matching the type you said you'd prefer.
explain.typeMatchDrum: It's a drum (front-load) machine, matching the type you said you'd prefer.
explain.quiet: At {{db}}dB during spin, it's one of the quieter picks here — good if your walls are thin or you tend to do laundry at night.
explain.valuePick: At {{price}}, it's the most affordable machine that still meets your conditions.
explain.premiumPick: It's a higher-end pick with the most complete feature set among your matches.
explain.capacityBelow: At {{kg}}kg, this is smaller than what's usually recommended for {{household}} — worth checking it covers your typical laundry load before choosing it over a larger model.
explain.capacityAbove: At {{kg}}kg, this is larger than what you were looking for, but smaller options didn't rank as well once your other conditions were factored in.
explain.dryMismatchHeatPump: This model doesn't have heat-pump drying — none of the machines that fit your entered space do, so this is the closest match on everything else.
explain.dryMismatchSimple: This model has no drying function at all — none of the machines that fit your entered space include one.
explain.typeMismatchVertical: This is a vertical (top-load) machine rather than the drum type you selected, but it's among the few options that fit your entered space.
explain.typeMismatchDrum: This is a drum (front-load) machine rather than the vertical type you selected, but it's among the few options that fit your entered space.
explain.lidFits: Its lid-open height ({{mm}}mm) is confirmed to clear the ceiling/shelf limit you entered.
explain.lidUnknown: We couldn't confirm this model's lid-open height (the clearance needed above it for the lid to fully open) — check the manufacturer's installation manual before relying on it against your ceiling or shelf limit.

recommend.lidCaution: Note: some of these results don't have a confirmed lid-open height, so we couldn't fully check them against your ceiling/shelf limit — look for the ⚠️ note on each one and check the manufacturer's installation manual before buying.

old.tapHelperTitle: Not sure if it's single or mixer?
old.tapHelperBody: Check for a small model code printed or embossed right on the tap body, then search "<code> 水栓" (or "<code> faucet") online — it'll usually say which type it is. Example: TOTO's TW11R / TW11GR (the common "Pitatto-kun" one-touch tap) is a single, cold-water-only tap with a one-touch hose connector and an emergency shut-off valve — by far the most common type in Japanese rentals.

guide.heading: Quick buying guide
guide.panBody: Compare using the pan's inner (usable) dimensions, not the machine's outer size. 640×640mm is by far the most common.
guide.typeBody: Vertical (top-load) machines open from the top, wash powerfully with strong water flow, stay compact, cost less, and are usually lighter for delivery. Drum (front-load) machines open from the front, use less water, and often dry better (especially heat-pump models), but are usually deeper, heavier, pricier, and need clear floor space in front for the door to swing open. If you're replacing an old top-load machine, a top-load replacement is usually the easier, safer-fitting choice.
guide.tapBody: Most rentals only have a cold-water single tap. Even machines with a warm-wash feature usually run fine in normal mode on a single tap — the warm feature just won't be available.
guide.capacityBody: Living alone: 5–7kg. Couple: 7–8kg. Family of 3+: 9kg or more.
guide.lidBody: For a top-load machine, what matters isn't just the closed body height — it's the extra height needed for the lid to swing fully open. If there's a shelf, vent fan, or low ceiling above your install spot, check that figure specifically, not just the body height. We flag it in the comparison whenever we don't have a confirmed number for a model.
guide.adsBody: Drum (front-load) washer-dryers cost more and market well as premium, automatic, and stylish — "wash to dry overnight." That doesn't mean they're always the better pick: for many Japanese apartments, a top-load machine is cheaper, lighter, easier to install, and washes just as well. Choose based on what actually fits your space and budget, not the ad copy.
